items.title: Robert Pattinson Named the Next James Bond—Months After Joking His Beverly Hills Move Made Him ‘Bougie’
items.summary:
Robert Pattinson is taking over as James Bond —months after the British actor revealed that he and Suki Waterhouse had traded Los Angeles ’ east side for a rental in Beverly Hills . 

The 40-year-old will succeed Daniel Craig in the 26th Bond film, becoming the seventh actor to play 007 in the official series.

Denis Villeneuve will direct the still-untitled movie, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay and Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing. Craig last appeared as the British spy in 2021’s "No Time to Die."

Five months before the casting announcement, Pattinson told GQ that he, Waterhouse, and their young daughter were renting a house in Beverly Hills. 

(Laurent KOFFEL/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images) 

The move took him to a part of town where he said he’d never lived. In his earlier years in Los Angeles, he owned a large home in Los Feliz, which he eventually sold. 

“I always thought I was an Eastside hipster guy. I would only ever come to Beverly Hills for my agency and stuff. Now I'm like, everything's kind of nice. Maybe I've turned bougie," he told the outlet. 

One feature of the rental had a practical purpose: its home gym. Pattinson told GQ he was using it to train for "The Batman: Part II," the sequel to his 2022 debut as the superhero. 

He recalled working out twice a day during preparations for his first turn as Batman and said that comments he’d made in interviews had given some people the wrong impression about how much he trained.

“[People said,] ‘You didn't work out at all.' I worked out every f—ing day. Even after that, I still look like I didn't…
items.t: Robert Pattinson Named the Next James Bond—Months After Joking His Beverly Hills Move Made Him ‘Bougie’

items.title: Contractor at Site of Brooklyn Building Collapse Was Previously Sued for Negligence
items.summary:
The general contractor overseeing the construction site adjacent to a deadly building collapse in Brooklyn was previously accused in a lawsuit of compromising the structural integrity of nearby properties during an excavation project, court records show.

Signage at the construction site at 2625 Bedford Ave., as well as planning documents filed with the Department of Buildings, show that Townhouse Builders, Inc, doing business as Promont, was the general contractor overseeing the construction project.

Building records show that the project involved excavation work directly adjacent to the three-story mixed-use building at 1321 Flatbush Ave. that fully collapsed on Wednesday, killing eight people, including two children, and leaving 18 others injured.

The construction project had a documented history of safety concerns flagged by DOB inspectors, and Mayor Zohran Mamdani says there will be a full investigation into whether any issues at the Bedford Ave. construction site contributed to the collapse.

"If there is anyone or any entity operating in this city that bears responsibility for what happened, we will hold them accountable," the mayor said.

Now, court records reviewed by Realtor.com® show that Townhouse Builders was accused in a 2020 lawsuit of causing "a breached wall, substantial shifting, settlement and cracking" to an adjacent property during a separate construction job.

New York state records list Mordachai Waisbrod as the CEO of Townhouse Builders. The company and an attorney listed as representing the Townhouse in the 2020 lawsuit did not respond to…
items.t: Contractor at Site of Brooklyn Building Collapse Was Previously Sued for Negligence

items.title: Mapped: Where the Most Homeowners Own Their Homes Outright With No Mortgage
items.summary:
Roughly 3 in 5 American homeowners pay a mortgage every month, yet the share of those who own their property outright is steadily growing—with at least half of all homeowners in three states now completely mortgage-free .

According to a new Realtor.com® data analysis of the recently released 2025 American Community Survey 1-Year Estimates , 59% of homeowners carried a mortgage last year, while 41% owned their homes free and clear.

That marks a major shift from 2010, when fewer than a third of homes (32.8%) were owned outright while 67% carried home loan debt.

Mortgaged homeownership has shrunk across all four regions, though reliance on financing still varies significantly by geography. The West had the highest mortgage debt rate at 63.8%, while the South recorded the lowest at 56.8%. The Northeast and Midwest tied at 58.7%.

At the state level, West Virginia led the nation with 56.6% of its homeowners living mortgage-free, followed by Mississippi (52.7%) and New Mexico (50%).

On the other side of the spectrum, Washington, DC , in 2025 logged the lowest share of outright homeownership, at just 26.5%, trailed by Maryland (30.6%) and Colorado (31.6%).

Realtor.com senior economist Jiayi Xu explains that the balance between mortgaged and free-and-clear homes meaningfully shapes housing market dynamics, especially at a time when mortgage rates are high.

"Areas where owners rely more heavily on mortgages are more sensitive to rate changes, because monthly payments and the cost of moving both rise with borrowing costs," says Xu. "Areas with a higher share of outright…
items.t: Mapped: Where the Most Homeowners Own Their Homes Outright With No Mortgage

items.title: America’s Trillion-Dollar Credit Card Debt Threatens To Lock Millions Out of the Housing Market
items.summary:
With prices still alarmingly high, it comes as no surprise that Americans are increasingly turning to credit cards more than ever. 

But doing so could be silently sabotaging any hope of owning a home , if you’re not careful. 

Last week, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York published its latest household debt report .

Collectively, credit card balances climbed by $22 billion in the third quarter to a record $1.29 trillion. Balances are up 4.2% from a year earlier, and total household debt, including mortgages, auto loans, and student loans, expanded by $334 billion for the period to a record $19.1 trillion.

High levels of debt are problematic for anyone, but most especially for first-time homebuyers. If your ambitions for 2027 include buying a home, it’s important to get your debt in check before it’s too late.

Easy money comes at a price 

According to TransUnion’s most recent quarterly credit industry insights report , the number of people with credit cards rose 2% to 178 million up from 174.8 million.

The ease of use means most people turn to credit cards for their everyday purchases, like groceries, gas, and utility bills—all of which have seen a steep increase in prices over the past two years. 

Now, if you’re someone who pays off their credit card in full each month, you’re in the clear. If not, the average interest rate on a new credit card offer currently stands at about 24%, and debt can accumulate quickly. 

And this can cause an array of issues for first-time homebuyers. 

"Issues arising from high levels of consumer debt are amplified for first-time…
items.t: America’s Trillion-Dollar Credit Card Debt Threatens To Lock Millions Out of the Housing Market

items.title: How Training Veterans in Skilled Trades Could Speed Up Homebuilding and Ease Housing Costs
items.summary:
A severe shortage of skilled workers entering the residential construction sector has had a major impact on affordability, but the Home Builders Institute (HBI) believes the country’s large veteran population may be part of the solution.

The skilled labor shortage has led to an increase in construction time, with each home taking nearly two months longer to build, according to an HBI study . Due to the delays, there was a reduction of 19,000 homes built in 2024, representing an economic loss of over $8 billion, the study found.

Associated Builders and Contractors (ABC) estimated that the construction industry needs to attract roughly 349,000 net new workers in 2026 and 456,000 new workers in 2027 to meet demand for construction services.

There are a number of factors in the past 30 years that have led to the labor shortage, according to HBI CEO Ed Brady . First, a strong push for four-year degrees led many young people toward academic careers rather than trades. With more people retiring from the workforce than entering, the shortage began.

The issue was compounded during the financial crisis of 2008, when the residential construction field lost tons of skilled workers because there wasn’t enough work. Without enough housing construction, workers left for jobs in manufacturing and hospitality or retired early, according to Brady.

More recently, rocky immigration policies have challenged the skilled labor workforce, Brady explains.

When finding a solution to the shortage became dire, HBI believed that the veteran and transitioning military population was “an untapped…
items.t: How Training Veterans in Skilled Trades Could Speed Up Homebuilding and Ease Housing Costs

items.title: Las Vegas Is Running Short on $100K-a-Month Rentals as A-Listers and Athletes Drive Demand
items.summary:
While Las Vegas drowns in unsold homes and priced-out buyers sit on the sidelines waiting for lower mortgage rates , the luxury rental sector is booming, fueled by visiting celebrities, professional athletes, and out-of-town millionaires eyeing a permanent move. 

In October, Las Vegas’ overall housing inventory reached an all-time high of nearly 11,450 units, up roughly 10% compared to a year ago, as mortgage rates topping 7% left many buyers priced out. 

Yet at the very top of the local rental market, the exact opposite is happening. 

Local brokers say that demand for rental mansions in Las Vegas and neighboring Henderson, NV , priced between $50,000 to $100,000 per month is severely outstripping supply.

"In the ultraluxury rental space, there's a huge shortage," Natalia Harris , global real estate adviser with Las Vegas Sotheby's International Realty , tells Realtor.com® . There are currently fewer than 10 super-luxury rentals on the market.

"We personally, day to day, feel the frustrations of the shortage of the inventory of these rentals, because we get requests and we can't even keep up with them."

Harris and her husband, fellow Sotheby's adviser Ben Harris , have been actively encouraging developers and investors to create more extravagant rental inventory to keep up with demand.

Well-heeled medium-term renters, including NFL stars and elite entertainers with $1 million-per-show residencies on the iconic Vegas Strip, are not just looking for a place to sleep. They crave complete privacy, top-of-the-line accommodations, and customized features ranging from…
items.t: Las Vegas Is Running Short on $100K-a-Month Rentals as A-Listers and Athletes Drive Demand

items.title: Sellers Are Cutting Home Prices the Most in These Markets—Led by One ‘Weirdly Nice’ City
items.summary:
As the market slowed in October due to seasonal trends and elevated mortgage rates , more than 1 in 5 listings throughout the country saw a price reduction, the highest October level since 2022.

For a few major metros, the share of price-reduced homes has pulled significantly ahead of the national share of listings with price reductions, which stood at 20.5%.

Price reductions were most common in Salt Lake City , where a whopping 31.8% of listings had price cuts as of October. The median listing price in October was $559,000 in Salt Lake City, a 3.5% decrease from October 2025, according to the Realtor.com economic research team’s monthly housing trends report .

The share of price-reduced homes in Salt Lake City increased 1.6 percentage points over last October.

Salt Lake City is followed closely by Indianapolis , where 31.7% of homes have had a price reduction, and Denver , with 30.9%.

Of the 50 largest metro areas in the U.S., these 10 had the largest share of price reductions in October:

Salt Lake City, UT: 31.8% 

Indianapolis, IN: 31.7% 

Denver, CO: 30.9% 

Portland, OR: 3.6% 

Phoenix, AZ: 29.5% 

Columbus, OH: 27.6% 

Charlotte, NC: 27.1%

items.title: Homeowner’s Massive 60,000-Light Christmas Display Dubbed a Safety Hazard by HOA
items.summary:
'Tis almost the season for goodwill toward all—unless you’re Neil Heuer and his neighbors.

Heuer, a semiretired tech entrepreneur, lives in Aero Plantation , an exclusive fly-in community in Waxhaw, NC , with his wife and their children. Over the past several months, he’s been locked in a battle with Aero Plantation's HOA over his annual Halloween and Christmas displays, which his neighbors say disrupt the neighborhood and make them feel unsafe. 

Heuer has been putting on the light shows, which include more than 60,000 lights, choreographed animatronic displays, and coordinated music programming, for the past five years. He estimates he's spent more than $70,000 on the exhibitions. 

But after last year’s shows, his neighbors began complaining. Those complaints led to a hearing, a lawsuit, and proposed potential changes to the HOA’s bylaws that would prohibit Heuer’s Christmas and Halloween spectaculars in the future. 

For his part, Heuer believes the drama has little to do with the lights and more to do with a golf course dispute and a once-anonymous newsletter he penned to bring HOA issues to light. 

"I realize that this is a little unorthodox, but, you know, everybody celebrates things differently," Heuer says of his light displays. "I have friends that celebrate their birthday for the entire month and I might be lucky to have a slice of cake on my birthday, but it doesn't matter. This is my hobby. I love to share it with people. I sit outside and record it myself, and I smile. I'm just so giddy with it.

"It makes me happy, which is good," he continues. "Especially…
items.t: Homeowner’s Massive 60,000-Light Christmas Display Dubbed a Safety Hazard by HOA

items.title: Thanksgiving Is the Worst Day of the Year for Cooking Fires—Is Your Kitchen Prepared?
items.summary:
If you’re hosting loved ones this Thanksgiving, now is the time to get your kitchen ready. Otherwise, a nice holiday meal could turn into a costly and dangerous ordeal. 

According to the latest data from the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) , about 1,139 home cooking fires were reported to U.S. fire departments on Thanksgiving Day 2024. 

That’s a 321% increase over the daily average, making Turkey Day the leading day of the year for home cooking fires.

“People don’t ever set out to leave the kitchen unattended, but a minute is all it takes for a grease and oil fire to take over, and there’s a greater risk of that happening on Thanksgiving when every burner is going,” says Payton Kashani , personal injury attorney, president, and managing partner of Sunset West Legal Group PC in Los Angeles .

By preparing your kitchen ahead of time, you can reduce the risk of fires and enjoy a delicious and safe celebration with family.

Why cooking fires spike on Thanksgiving 

The NFPA says that unattended cooking is the leading cause of home cooking fires. And that’s quite common on Thanksgiving Day.

Many dishes are usually being cooked at once on the stove, oven, and various countertop appliances. Add in a house full of guests that bring constant interruptions and you’re left with a risky situation.

“Thanksgiving fires aren’t usually about cooking appliances going wrong. They tend to happen in those few minutes when someone steps away to greet a guest at the door. Distractions like this can wind up causing serious burns with long, painful recoveries that shake up a…
items.t: Thanksgiving Is the Worst Day of the Year for Cooking Fires—Is Your Kitchen Prepared?

items.title: Spain’s Housing Crisis Sparks a Revolt Against Tourism. Could America Feel the Fallout?
items.summary:
Millions of workers walked off the job across Spain on Wednesday, demanding relief from soaring rents , evictions, and housing speculation. It was the the country's first general strike in 14 years.

In Barcelona, protesters rattled house keys and chanted, “ O baixen els lloguers, o cremen els carrers ," which translates to “Either rents fall, or the streets burn.”

Over the past decade, rents in the City of Counts have climbed more than 50% , with tourism adding pressure on an already strained housing market .

In the coastal city of Málaga, Mónica Reino , 56, has watched that transformation unfold in her own apartment building.

“Every year it gets worse,” she told AFP , estimating that half of its 20 apartments are now tourist accommodations.

Tourism is far from the only force driving Spain's housing crisis. In popular vacation destinations, property owners can earn more from short-term visitors than year-round tenants, creating a financial incentive to convert residential housing into tourist accommodations .

A day after the strike, lawmakers narrowly approved a package of housing measures , including a new 10% tax on qualifying vacation rentals.

The conflict mirrors one already playing out in vacation destinations across the United States, where booming tourism has helped sustain local economies while putting housing increasingly out of reach for residents.

But as restrictions on vacation rentals make accommodations scarcer and more expensive abroad, could more travelers turn to U.S. destinations, intensifying the housing pressures those communities are already…
items.t: Spain’s Housing Crisis Sparks a Revolt Against Tourism. Could America Feel the Fallout?

items.title: Jackson, MS Struggles with Low Starter Home Availability Compared to Other Cities
items.summary:
For many prospective homeowners, the search for an affordable starter home can feel like a daunting task. A recent analysis by Realtor.com® explores the changing landscape of entry-level housing across the country, revealing where these crucial properties are becoming more or less common.

Nationally, starter home options have felt increasingly scarce as rising prices and climbing mortgage rates compound the challenge. According to research, the national share of starter homes in active inventory fell from 38.1% in August 2019 to 36.2% in August 2026. Moreover, during that same period, starter home prices rose 30.8%, from roughly $260,000 to $340,000.

As a result, some markets have seen a significant shift in their housing stock. 

In Jackson, MS , the availability of starter homes has experienced a slight downturn in recent years, reflecting the broader challenges facing many homebuyers.

Starter home availability dips slightly in jackson 

A starter home is defined by Realtor.com as a property priced at roughly 80% of a metro's median list price, which captures the relative affordability of the lower end of each local market. These homes are typically smaller and less expensive, making them accessible to a first-time buyer or a household with an income at or below the area median.

In Jackson, the share of starter homes was 36.4% in 2019 and rose to 38.6% in 2022. However, by 2026, the share had decreased to 36.3% of the market's available inventory.

Therefore, this represents a -0.1 point change between 2019 and 2026. This slight decline indicates a modest tightening…
items.t: Jackson, MS Struggles with Low Starter Home Availability Compared to Other Cities
